question.problem:
Which of the following linear congruences do **NOT** have any solutions?

I. $10x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,36)$

II. $5x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,36)$

III. $4x≡18\,(\text{mod}\,36)$
question.worked_solution:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14269988/assets/b65fc4830e0b060d62226b41d5ccb7bdc63d0ad594f7a42a2628597409bba3af.png)

      

Recall the following facts regarding the congruence $ax≡b\,(\text{mod}\,n):$

- The congruence has no solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,\text{⧸}|\,b.
$$

- The congruence has $\text{gcd}(a,n)$ solutions modulo $n$ if and only if 

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)\,|\,b.
$$

With that in mind, let's examine our congruences.

- Congruence I has two solutions modulo $36.$ We have $a=10$ and $n=36$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(10,36)=2.
$$

Since $b=18$ is divisible by $2,$ this congruence has $2$ solutions.

- Congruence II has a unique solution modulo $36.$ We have $a=5$ and $n=36$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(5,36)=1.
$$

Therefore, this congruence has a unique solution.

- Congruence III has no solutions. We have $a=4$ and $n=36$, and so

$$
\text{gcd}(a,n)=\text{gcd}(4,36)=4.
$$

Since $b=18$ is not divisible by $4,$ this congruence has no solutions.

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only".
